transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SDR); Maya Chen (AtlasRetail), Carlos Rivera (AtlasRetail), Leah Ortiz (AtlasRetail)

Summary:
Redwood hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for AtlasRetail's product search relevance. Discussed integration options, performance/cost tradeoffs, security/compliance, and next steps for a 1-week pilot.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and vector dimensions
- Reranking endpoint: two-stage search flow (ANN + rerank)
- Latency vs batching vs cost tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment options briefly
- Evaluation: metrics (MRR, NDCG), sample dataset, A/B approach

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Blake, AE at Redwood. Today Priya and I will run through our hosted embeddings and reranking flow, show some sample responses and talk pilot options.
[00:09] Maya: Hi Jordan, thanks. We had a quick internal sync — I'm Maya, head of search, and Carlos here runs the model stuff. We're most concerned about relevance and keeping latency under 150ms for top results.
[00:20] Carlos: Yup and also data residency, we need to make sure PII never leaves our region, and encryption at rest with our K M S.
[00:28] Priya: Great, we'll cover that. Quick show of hands — are you using an existing vector store or looking for recommendations?
[00:33] Leah: We currently use Elastic's vector plugin for similarity search, but results are noisy; we do a hybrid approach with filters then simple score.
[00:40] Priya: Perfect. So our recommended flow for product search is a two-stage pipeline: stage one — lightweight ANN or filter to produce candidates using embeddings, stage two — our reranker endpoint that takes the top K (we typically demo K=50) and returns re-scored ranked list.
[00:54] Jordan: I'll share my screen — quick deck link: https://redwood.com/decks/hosted-embeddings.pdf (also sending in chat).
[01:02] [screen share noise] Priya: Here's the embeddings endpoint: you POST product descriptions or queries, receive 1024-d embedding vectors by default for the model we show. You can choose smaller dims or quantized variants to reduce cost.
[01:16] Carlos: 1024 dims — what about payload size and tokenization? If I batch 100 queries, what's the latency like?
[01:23] Priya: Good question. For hosted, typical single-request latency for embeddings is ~40-80ms depending on model and sequence length; batching 100 can increase throughput but will add a bit of latency — we do continuous batching in our runtime to avoid tail spikes. For rerank, because it needs context and cross-attention, it's heavier — expect ~120-250ms depending on K and model.
[01:39] Maya: So would that put us over our 150ms SLO for frontend?
[01:42] Jordan: Usually we recommend doing ANN for the initial pass to keep frontend under SLO, then rerank asynchronously for quality-sensitive use cases or do a tiny re-rank (K=10) inline. Also you can use our lower-latency quantized model variants for reranking to get closer to 150ms.
[01:55] Carlos: Any tradeoffs in quality with quantized models?
[01:58] Priya: Minimal for rerank tasks usually — we provide model profiles and evals. We can run your test set and show delta; that's part of the pilot.
[02:06] Maya: Security — you mentioned K M S and V P C earlier. We need SOC2, SSO and audit logs to satisfy legal.
[02:12] Jordan: We're SOC2 Type II, we enforce SSO via SAML, RBAC, and offer private deployments for customers needing VPC or on-prem. For hosted we have encryption at rest and KMS integrations. I'll share the security packet after the call.
[02:23] Leah: Do you support regional endpoints? Data residency is a must for EU.
[02:26] Priya: Yes, we have region routing and can pin requests to specific regions. For strict residency we'd recommend Private deployment or Dedicated depending on volume.
[02:34] Carlos: How do you handle prefix caching/K V cache? We rely on cache to avoid repeating expensive reranks for repeated queries.
[02:40] Priya: We have KV cache and prefix caching; sometimes transcripts show it as K V cash in logs, haha — but it's caching of the key-value attention cache. That reduces token compute on repeated sessions for chat; for rerank caching of candidate embeddings is common.
[02:54] Jordan: Let's run a short demo — we have a sample product catalog and query set. I'll call the embeddings endpoint for a sample query and then the reranker for the top 20.
[03:04] [demo noise — typing]
[03:10] Jordan: Embeddings request posted — here are nearest neighbors from the vector store (we're simulating vector store locally). You can see the initial candidates include some category-mismatches. Now running reranker with context, you can see top results reorder and improve NDCG visually.
[03:28] Maya: Looks promising, did you tune for business rules like promotions and availability?
[03:33] Priya: Yes, the reranker supports structured context and metadata signals. You can pass availability, price, and promotional boosts as features; the model accepts those and we provide a structured prompt format.
[03:44] Carlos: For evaluation, what metrics do you recommend? We run MRR and NDCG now.
[03:49] Priya: MRR, NDCG at cutoff 10, relevance@k; also measure average latency P95 end-to-end. We'll help set up an eval harness as part of the pilot.
[03:58] Jordan: Pricing — hosted is usage-based: per-embedding unit and per-rerank call token-based. I'll send a sample estimate for 10k queries/day and a couple of model profiles.
[04:08] Leah: Any limitations on throughput for hosted? We might have spikes during promotions.
[04:12] Priya: For spikes we have burst capacity and autoscaling. For consistent heavy throughput we recommend Dedicated. Hosted handles bursty traffic but with soft capacity limits and rate limits depending on contract.
[04:22] Carlos: What about log access and audit for compliance?
[04:25] Jordan: We provide audit logs, per-request metadata, and retention config; advanced retention is an add-on. We'll include the specific fields you can export.
[04:33] Maya: Great. I want to summarize next steps — Jordan to share pricing and security docs; Priya to propose pilot config and evaluation plan; Carlos to send sample catalog and current metrics.
[04:44] Jordan: Yup, and we'll target a pilot start next week pending approvals.
[04:47] Maya: Sounds good, thanks.
[04:49] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the pilot contract.
[04:53] [call ends]
